conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
CONCENTRATION CELL NOTATION

M(s) | Mⁿ⁺(aq, C₁) || Mⁿ⁺(aq, C₂) | M(s)

Anode:   M(s) ──► Mⁿ⁺(C₁) + ne⁻
Cathode: Mⁿ⁺(C₂) + ne⁻ ──► M(s)
Net:     Mⁿ⁺(C₂) ⇌ Mⁿ⁺(C₁)

E_cell = (0.05916 / n) log₁₀ (C₂ / C₁)
conceptBreakdown.content:
A Concentration Cell consists of identical electrodes immersed in solutions of the same electrolyte at different concentrations ($C_1 \neq C_2$).
• Because the electrodes are identical, $\mathbf{E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 0}$.
• The cell potential is driven solely by concentration gradient: $\mathbf{E_{\text{cell}} = \frac{0.05916}{n} \log_{10} \left( \frac{C_2}{C_1} \right)}$.
• For spontaneous discharge, $\mathbf{C_2 > C_1}$ (cathode concentration must be higher than anode).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
HYDROGEN CONCENTRATION CELL & pH

Pt | H₂(1 bar) | H⁺(pH₁) || H⁺(pH₂) | H₂(1 bar) | Pt

E_cell = 0.05916 × log₁₀ ([H⁺]₂ / [H⁺]₁) = 0.05916 × (pH₁ - pH₂)
conceptBreakdown.content: Hydrogen concentration cells are used in electrochemical $\text{pH}$ meters. If the cathode is standard $1.0\text{ M } \text{H}^+$ ($\text{pH} = 0$), then $E_{\text{cell}} = 0.05916 \times \text{pH}_{\text{anode}}$.
